title: Operation Shadowfall
question: What should be handed over first when one service has a scoped action and another has an unresolved coverage gap?
briefing: A settlement session, a customer-service coverage gap and a routine lab review compete for attention. You can make a useful prioritised handoff without claiming certainty about all three. Your authority is to acquire records and recommend a session-scoped response through Coordinated Response. You cannot approve your own control or disable an entire account or service.
lesson: A prioritised handoff separates supported findings, remaining uncertainty, owners and next review triggers.

entities.name: Named settlement-service session
entities.impact: Settlement is a live business dependency. The customer-service coverage gap has a separate restoration owner; it cannot be silently cleared by a settlement finding.
entities.capability: Named session and disclosed source paths only; no account-wide or host-wide control.
entities.dependency: Settlement is a live business dependency. The customer-service coverage gap has a separate restoration owner; it cannot be silently cleared by a settlement finding.

entities.name: COVERAGE-12 context
entities.purpose: Related context that must be assessed separately
entities.impact: Do not generalise the primary session finding to this separate scope.
entities.capability: Only the explicitly delivered relationship and source records.
entities.dependency: A separate task or observation does not supply approval for the primary session.

entities.name: Isolated test lab
entities.impact: No live customer service depends on this lab review.
entities.dependency: Not a dependency of settlement or customer-service collection.

mechanic.question: What should be handed over first when one service has a scoped action and another has an unresolved coverage gap?

options.label: Wait for certainty about every system before making any handoff
Prioritise the settlement finding and retain a separate coverage-restoration task
Use one explained action to declare the environment clean

limits.label: A scoped settlement finding neither resolves the independent historical coverage gap nor clears the entire environment.
Unavailable collection does not establish that no activity occurred.
The source identifies a session or credential, not a person or motive.
Other scopes and their remaining questions need their own evidence.

queries.label: Establish the task and business consequence
queries.question: What is this service for, and which consequences change investigation priority?
queries.can: Names the normal task, related scopes, owners and interruption consequence.
queries.cannot: Does not establish who performed the current action.

queries.label: Check the exact work authorisation
queries.question: Does approved work cover this session, task, target and period?
queries.cannot: Does not prove the human operator or the activity that actually occurred.

queries.label: Inspect the scoped session activity
queries.question: Which action was recorded for this named session within collection limits?
queries.can: Records session-level actions and the observed target.
queries.cannot: Cannot identify a person, establish motive or reconstruct missing historical collection.

queries.label: Check the service transaction independently
queries.question: Does the service-side transaction establish the same scoped operation?
queries.can: Tests the operation through a separately collected service transaction.
queries.cannot: A second card alone does not establish a sufficient explanation.

facts.title: Starting observations
facts.text: A settlement session, a customer-service coverage gap and a routine lab review compete for attention. You can make a useful prioritised handoff without claiming certainty about all three.

facts.title: Task, scope and business consequence
facts.text: The settlement service has immediate customer-payment consequence. COVERAGE-12 lacks privileged application collection from authored event steps -3 through 0; authentication-only records cannot fill that interval. Detection Engineering owns restoration and a repeat verification within four steps. The lab is an isolated planned test. The disclosed priority is settlement scope, then coverage restoration; the lab can remain routine.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The settlement work order approves this session’s reconciliation read. It does not address the separate customer-service collection gap.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The settlement session performed the reconciliation read named in its work order. This explains that scoped action while the separate coverage-restoration handoff remains necessary.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The settlement journal independently confirms the approved reconciliation read for this session. It says nothing about the separate missing customer-service interval.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The settlement work order approves this session’s reconciliation read. It does not address the separate customer-service collection gap. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The settlement work order permits reconciliation reads only. No approval covers destination changes through this session. The independent collection gap remains a separate issue.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The settlement session submitted a payment-destination change outside its reconciliation role. This supports a scoped response while the customer-service coverage gap requires its own follow-up.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The payment workflow independently ties a destination-change request to the named settlement session, beyond the reconciliation work order.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The settlement work order permits reconciliation reads only. No approval covers destination changes through this session. The independent collection gap remains a separate issue. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: Work record unavailable
facts.text: The work-authorisation archive is unavailable for the named session and period. No approval or denial can be inferred.

facts.title: Session collection unavailable
facts.text: The session-audit source did not collect the relevant historical interval. Absence of a record cannot establish the absence of activity.

facts.title: Independent collection is limited
facts.text: The independent service journal lacks the target application operation for the historical interval. A different source name does not restore that capability.

facts.title: Verified check timed out
facts.text: The pre-established directory contact did not respond by the stated due step. This is a delivered limitation, not approval or a reason to wait indefinitely.

facts.title: A later scoped transaction
facts.text: The named session performed a further source-recorded operation within the specifically approved task. This later event does not identify the person, establish motive or change any earlier snapshot.

response.control: Restrict only the named organisation-controlled session
response.objective: A further out-of-scope operation completes through the same session if its access remains active.
response.dependency: Settlement is a live business dependency. The customer-service coverage gap has a separate restoration owner; it cannot be silently cleared by a settlement finding.

glossary.definition: A prioritised handoff separates supported findings, remaining uncertainty, owners and next review triggers.
The target, operation and interval a source is capable of observing.
The explicitly named session or service covered by a claim and next action.

reviewWindow: The named session from its start through the explicit cutoff of each acquired snapshot. A simulation step is an investigation opportunity, not a minute.
